messages:
Maya K.: Heads-up — during the private deploy preflight for acme-corp I noticed keystore audit entries missing for the rotation that ran last night. KMS API returned 200 but our auditd shows no principal or key-id entry. Anyone seen this pattern? :thinking:
Alex P.: hmm, do you mean the onprem keystore agent called the KMS but we don't have a local audit record? can you paste the agent logs? :eyes:
Maya K.: pasted logs below from redwood-keystore-agent pod (truncated):
```
2026-03-20T23:12:01Z INFO rotation: started key-rotate job id=rot-20260320-01
2026-03-20T23:12:02Z INFO kms_request result=200 operation=Encrypt key_id=projects/acme/locations/global/keyR
2026-03-20T23:12:02Z WARN audit_event=null principal=null
2026-03-20T23:12:02Z INFO rotation: completed id=rot-20260320-01
```
Maya K.: auditd on the host shows no corresponding event either (ausearch returns nothing for that timeframe).
sec-bot: ALERT: KMS_AUDIT_ANOMALY detected for cluster=acme-staging, severity=low-medium — missing audit events after KMS calls.
Lisa C.: could this be a netpol/eBPF egress issue? if the agent got 200 it's likely to be a proxied response, but maybe the sidecar that emits audit events couldn't reach the logging collector.
Ivan R.: quick checklist — 1) did someone change the serviceaccount/rolebinding used by keystore-agent? 2) did netpols block egress from the audit-forwarder? 3) did the host-level audit rules get replaced?
Maya K.: I ran `kubectl get roles,rolebindings -n redwood-keystore` and saw a new rolebinding added yesterday: `keystore-agent-readonly` bound to `keystore-agent-sa` with only `get` on secrets. previously the rolebinding granted `auditlogs.write` (custom).
Alex P.: ah that sounds promising — if the in-cluster forwarder lost write permission to the logging namespace, it might drop events after the KMS call. do we have the role YAML?
Maya K.: snippet from gitops commit (hash abc123):
```
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: keystore-agent-readonly
rules:
- apiGroups: ["logging.redwood.io"]
  resources: ["auditEvents"]
  verbs: ["get"]
```
Maya K.: previous role had `verbs: ["create","patch"]` and a label `redwood.com/audit-proxy: enabled`.
ops-runner: FYI I saw a netpol deny for pod=keystore-agent from network-plugin yesterday: `DENY egress to 10.1.8.9:443 (logging-collector)` — that was around 23:11 UTC.
Lisa C.: so two independent failures: RBAC downgrade for the forwarder + transient netpol deny. combo explains missing audit records despite successful KMS response (agent got response, forwarder couldn't persist event).
Ivan R.: escalate plan: mark as P2 triage (not data-exfil but breaks audit trail). immediate steps: 1) restore rolebinding to include create/patch for auditEvents 2) patch netpol to allow egress to logging-collector CIDR 10.1.8.0/24 for namespace redwood-keystore 3) re-run rotation simulation and verify audit entries.
Alex P.: I'll open an infra PR to restore role + add explicit egress allow for that namespace, tag @infra-team.
Alex P.: PR: https://git.company/acme/infrastructure/pulls/524 — restores role and adds netpol exception.
sec-bot: NOTE: created ticket SEC-2026-134 for missing-audit-events (linked to PR 524).
Maya K.: re-run verification commands after PR merge: 1) `kubectl exec -n redwood-keystore -c agent <pod> -- cat /var/log/keystore-agent.log | tail -n 50` 2) `kubectl logs -n logging logging-collector --since=1h | grep "auditEvent"` 3) `ausearch -m USER_AVC -ts 2026-03-20T23:00:00`
Ivan R.: after we merged the RBAC rollback and netpol exception (rolled out at 2026-03-21T00:03:22Z), I re-ran a simulated rotate and saw audit events appear with principal and key_id. sample from logging-collector: `{"ts":"2026-03-21T00:03:23Z","event":"auditEvent","principal":"serviceAccount:keystore-agent-sa","key_id":"projects/acme/locations/global/keyR","action":"rotate"}`
Lisa C.: good. action items: - add an automated canary that runs a test rotation every 6h and asserts that auditEvents show up within 30s - add an admission check preventing rolebindings that remove audit write verbs for namespaces labeled `redwood.com/keystore` - add netpol integration test in CI so netpol changes fail if they block egress to known logging collectors.
Maya K.: noted. I'll file followups in the incident ticket and attach the forensic logs. cc @ops-runner for postmortem timeline.
Alex P.: vuln triage note: this was an availability/observability regression, not a secrets exposure. mark low CVSS, but high-operational-impact.
ops-runner: closing loop — we've created SEC-2026-134, added PR 524, and scheduled postmortem for 2026-03-22 14:00 UTC. thanks team. :thumbsup:
